# superset_sql_execution (Resource)

Runs a SQL statement through SQL Lab on a database connection, for example to create a view or a table that a dataset is then built on. The statement runs when the resource is created and again whenever `triggers` change; a change of the statement, the connection, the schema or the catalog replaces the resource, which runs `destroy_sql` first when it is set. The connection must be exposed in SQL Lab (`expose_in_sqllab`) and allow DML (`allow_dml`) for a statement that changes data or structure. Several statements separated by `;` run in order; the rows a statement returns are discarded.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A view created through SQL Lab and dropped with the resource; the connection must allow DML.
# Bump the version to run the statement again.
resource "superset_sql_execution" "daily_sales" {
  database_name = "Warehouse"
  schema        = "public"
  sql           = "CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW daily_sales AS SELECT day, sum(amount) AS amount FROM sales GROUP BY day"
  destroy_sql   = "DROP VIEW IF EXISTS daily_sales"
  triggers = {
    version = "1"
  }
}

# The dataset on the view waits for it.
resource "superset_dataset" "daily_sales" {
  table_name    = "daily_sales"
  database_name = "Warehouse"
  schema        = "public"
  depends_on    = [superset_sql_execution.daily_sales]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `sql` (String) The statement to run.

### Optional

- `catalog` (String) Catalog to run in, on Superset 6 connections with several catalogs. Left to the default of the connection when unset.
- `database_id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the connection, looked up from `database_name` when that is set.
- `database_name` (String) Name of the database connection to run on. Exactly one of `database_name` and `database_id` must be set.
- `destroy_sql` (String) Statement run when the resource is destroyed or replaced, for example `DROP VIEW IF EXISTS daily_sales`. Nothing runs when unset, and nothing runs when the connection no longer exists.
- `schema` (String) Schema the unqualified names of the statement are resolved in.
- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values whose change runs the statement again, for example a version.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Identifier of the last run in the query history of SQL Lab.
